hero_lede: Service upgrades, panels, lighting, EV chargers, repairs and new-construction wiring for Logan Square and Bucktown two-flats, boulevard greystones, coach houses, new houses and Milwaukee Avenue storefronts. A family-owned, founder-led contractor licensed by the City of Chicago, quoting every job in writing.
boundary_text: Bounded by Diversey Avenue to the north, the Bloomingdale Trail (The 606) to the south, the Metra Milwaukee District North tracks near Pulaski Road to the west and the North Branch of the Chicago River to the east. It takes in Bucktown and Palmer Square as well as the landmark boulevards around the square, so blocks of new houses sit a few streets from greystones built before 1930.

districts.name: The square and Milwaukee Ave
districts.intro: The Illinois Centennial Monument circle, where Logan and Kedzie boulevards meet Milwaukee Ave by the Logan Square Blue Line station, and the storefront buildings with flats above that line Milwaukee.
districts.work: Restaurant, café and studio fit-outs, services for mixed-use buildings and work in the flats upstairs, scheduled around opening hours. Our record includes two restaurant renovations and a yoga studio on Milwaukee.

districts.name: The boulevards and Palmer Square
districts.intro: Logan, Kedzie, Palmer and Humboldt boulevards and Palmer Square Park: the Logan Square Boulevards District, a Chicago Landmark district since 2005, with greystones, large houses, apartment buildings and churches built from about 1880 to 1930.
districts.work: Service and panel upgrades in big older buildings, rewiring behind plaster and new lighting, with the City's landmark permit review for work on the buildings.

districts.name: California and The 606
districts.intro: Between Humboldt Blvd and Western Ave south of Fullerton, around the California Blue Line station and the Bloomingdale Trail: older flats side by side with new single-family houses and three-unit masonry buildings.
districts.work: New-construction wiring and service upgrades with new meters in the older flats. Many of our new-construction permits are on N Point St, N Mozart St, N Fairfield Ave and N Washtenaw Ave.

districts.name: Bucktown
districts.intro: Fullerton Ave south to The 606, between Western Ave and the Kennedy: older frame and brick houses mixed with new houses and small masonry buildings, with shops along Milwaukee and Armitage.
districts.work: New houses wired from plans, roof-deck and garage circuits, additions to older houses and EV chargers, on blocks such as N Wolcott Ave, W Lyndale St and W Shakespeare Ave.

districts.name: West of Kedzie
districts.intro: From Kedzie Ave west to the Metra tracks near Pulaski Rd, around Kosciuszko Park: streets of brick and frame two-flats, single-family houses and small apartment buildings.
districts.work: 60- and 100-amp services replaced with 200 amps and a new meter for each unit, basement and laundry circuits, and basement conversion units.

buildings.title: Two-, three- or four-flat
buildings.where: Throughout, especially west of Kedzie and around the boulevards
buildings.changes: The service is usually split between the units at a meter bank in the basement. Many still have 60- or 100-amp services, so an upgrade means 200 amps and a new meter and panel for every unit.

buildings.title: Boulevard greystone or large older house
buildings.where: Logan, Kedzie, Palmer and Humboldt boulevards and Palmer Square
buildings.changes: Buildings from about 1880 to 1930 with plaster walls, high ceilings and wiring that may date from several eras. They sit in a Chicago Landmark district, so permit applications also go through the City's Historic Preservation Division.

buildings.title: New single-family house
buildings.where: Bucktown and the blocks around The 606
buildings.changes: Built from plans, usually with a basement, a rooftop deck and stair enclosure, and a detached two-car garage off the alley that needs its own feed.

buildings.title: New two- to four-unit building
buildings.where: N Mozart St, W Lyndale St, N Kedzie Ave, N California Ave and W Armitage Ave
buildings.changes: Three-storey masonry buildings with a meter and panel for each unit, a house panel for the common areas, and roof decks and garages to wire.

buildings.title: Storefront, restaurant or studio
buildings.where: Milwaukee Ave, Armitage Ave and Fullerton Ave
buildings.changes: Often a two- or three-storey building with flats above, so a fit-out has to be powered without disturbing the tenants upstairs, and kitchens need heavy circuits.

buildings.title: Coach house or basement unit
buildings.where: Behind houses and two-flats across the area
buildings.changes: A coach house may be fed from the front building or need its own service, risers and weatherhead. A new basement conversion unit needs circuits of its own, and the City's ADU rules decide whether the unit is allowed.

scope_lede: The same job on paper can cost very differently in a boulevard greystone, a four-flat on 100 amps and a new Bucktown house. These are the things that change it, and most are settled at the walkthrough.
scope_rows: Permit applications for buildings in the Logan Square Boulevards District go through the City's Historic Preservation Division, so plan exterior changes such as a moved meter, a new service mast or façade lighting around that review.
Many two- and three-flats still run on 60- or 100-amp services. An EV charger, central air or a new basement unit can mean a 200-amp service, a meter for each unit and a ComEd appointment.
A service upgrade on a two-, three- or four-flat replaces every unit's meter and panel, so the unit count sets much of the scope.
Buildings from the 1880s to the 1920s can still hide fuse boxes, cloth-covered wire and old DIY repairs behind the walls.
Fishing wire through plaster and lath in a greystone or two-flat is slower than drywall and needs careful patching.
A coach house can run from the front building or need its own service, risers and weatherhead, which ComEd can ask for before it upgrades a service.
Many houses have a garage off the alley. A feed for an EV charger can mean trenching and new conduit from the house panel.
A new house or small building is wired from the architect's drawings, with roof-deck, garage and unit-meter details settled before rough-in.
Your architect or builder, with us
On Milwaukee Ave a shop or restaurant often shares its building with the flats upstairs, which shapes how a fit-out is powered and when the work can happen.
Restaurants and occupied flats often need work planned around service hours or tenants, so agree the hours before the job is booked.
Service upgrades, EV circuits and unit work usually go through the City's Express Permit Program. New buildings and fit-outs need plans and a fuller review.
hourly_answer: We quote by scope, not by the hour, because the hours on a Logan Square job depend on the factors below. A new circuit in a Bucktown house built ten years ago and the same circuit behind the plaster of a boulevard greystone aren't the same job. The written quote tells you the whole price before you agree to it.
choosing_building_why: A boulevard greystone, an older two-flat on 60 amps, a new Bucktown house with a roof deck and a Milwaukee Ave storefront are four different jobs.
choosing_building_answer: About 120 City of Chicago permits in Logan Square since 2012: new houses and two- to four-unit buildings in Bucktown and around The 606, service upgrades with new meters in two-, three- and four-flats west of the boulevards, and restaurant and studio fit-outs on Milwaukee Ave
choosing_paperwork_why: Buildings on the boulevards go through the City's landmark permit review, and new houses and fit-outs need plans approved before the permit is issued.
where_we_fit: Highlights is a family-owned contractor. In Logan Square we're the right call for two-flats, greystones, coach houses, new houses and small buildings: service upgrades, panels, rewiring, lighting, EV chargers, and restaurant and shop fit-outs on Milwaukee Ave. Base-building work for the large retail stores on Elston Ave is a job for the big commercial firms, and we'll tell you so.

honest_context: Logan Square is one of the areas we work in most. Most of our roughly 1,200 Chicago permits are in Wards 1, 32, 26, 47 and 27, and Logan Square is mostly the 1st and 32nd, so about 120 of them, roughly one in ten, are here. Most came from the run of new houses and two- to four-unit buildings in Bucktown and around The 606 from 2013 to 2021. Since then the work has been service upgrades, EV chargers, renovations and fit-outs.

Logan Square is busy: about 940 permits with electrical work in the last two years, naming about 300 electrical contractors. Much of it is the same kind of work as ours, in the same older flats and houses. The mix also includes illuminated signs for shops on Elston Ave and rooftop solar, and our own Logan Square record has no sign or solar permits.

faq: Do I need landmark approval for electrical work on a Logan Square boulevard?

If your building is in the Logan Square Boulevards District, a Chicago Landmark district since 2005 along Logan, Kedzie, Palmer and Humboldt boulevards, the City's Historic Preservation Division reviews permit applications for work on it. The review checks that the work won't harm the building's historic features, so exterior changes such as moving a meter, a new service mast or façade lighting are the ones to plan around. Our own record includes a restaurant renovation in the district on W Armitage Ave.
Can you upgrade the electrical service on my two-flat or three-flat?

Yes. It's one of our most common Logan Square jobs: replacing a 60- or 100-amp service with 200 amps and a new meter and panel for each unit. Our permits here include four-meter upgrades on N Avers Ave, N Monticello Ave and N Mozart St, and we arrange the ComEd side of the job.
Can you wire a coach house or a basement conversion unit?

Yes, including a conversion unit in a two-flat on W Wrightwood Ave. The first question is whether the existing service can carry another unit or needs to be upgraded. The City's Additional Dwelling Unit rules decide whether the unit itself is allowed on your lot.
Do you wire new houses and small buildings in Bucktown and Logan Square?

Yes. About half of our Logan Square permits are new construction: single-family houses and two- to four-unit masonry buildings, many with rooftop decks and detached garages. We work from the architect's drawings, pull the electrical permit and see it through inspection.
Can you put an EV charger in my garage off the alley?

Usually, yes. Most chargers need one new circuit. If the garage is detached, the feed runs from the house panel, which can mean trenching, and if the service can't carry the charger the upgrade comes first. Our Logan Square record includes charger circuits on N Milwaukee Ave, N Drake Ave and N Spaulding Ave.
Which Logan Square ZIP codes do you cover?
All of them. Most of Logan Square is 60647, and its edges fall in 60614, 60618, 60622 and 60639. We cover every other Chicago neighbourhood too.
